paragraphs.title: Wisdom, Obedience, and the Limits of Control

easy.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:1 says, "a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine."
easy.q: What makes a man's face shine?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, "I counsel thee to keep the king's commandment."
easy.q: Whose commandment does the writer counsel people to keep?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that no man has power "over the spirit to retain the spirit."

answers: The meaning or understanding of it
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to understanding the meaning of a matter.
medium.q: What does "the interpretation of a thing" refer to in verse 1?

answers: Because he cannot know what shall be or control the day of death
Because the king has no authority
medium.explanation: Verses 7–8 stress that a person does not know the future and has no power over death.
medium.q: Why should a person recognize the limits of his control?

answers: Keeping the commandment removes all judgment
Keeping the commandment gives control over the spirit
A wise heart discerns both time and judgment
medium.explanation: Verse 5 connects keeping the commandment with a wise heart that discerns time and judgment.
medium.q: How are keeping the commandment and wisdom connected?

answers: Between obedience to authority and the limits of human control
challenge.explanation: The passage calls for obedience to the king while also showing that people cannot control the future, death, or the spirit.
challenge.q: What central tension appears in verses 1–8?

answers: Wickedness cannot ultimately protect its followers
Wickedness gives power over the spirit
challenge.explanation: Verse 8 teaches that wickedness cannot deliver a person from human limitations or death.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the statement, "neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it"?

answers: Wisdom gives complete control over the future
Wisdom is unnecessary for understanding life
Wisdom enlightens a person but does not remove uncertainty
challenge.explanation: Wisdom makes the face shine, yet the passage still says that no one knows what shall be.
challenge.q: How does the passage describe the relationship between wisdom and certainty?

paragraphs.title: Power, the Wicked, and Injustice in the World

answers: It is to his own hurt
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says there is a time when "one man ruleth over another to his own hurt."
easy.q: What happens when one man rules over another?

answers: Because judgment against evil is not executed speedily
Because they have too much joy
easy.explanation: Verse 11 gives the delay of judgment as the reason people become committed to evil.
easy.q: Why is the heart of the sons of men fully set to do evil?

easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, "it shall be well with them that fear God."
easy.q: For whom does Qohelet say it shall be well?

answers: Because punishment does not come quickly
Because there are no consequences in life
medium.explanation: The delayed execution of judgment causes the hearts of people to become set on doing evil.
medium.q: Why might people encourage themselves to do evil?

answers: The righteous receive what belongs to the wicked, and the wicked receive what belongs to the righteous
Everyone receives exactly what he deserves
medium.explanation: Verse 14 describes a vanity in which outcomes do not always match a person's conduct.
medium.q: What injustice is described in verse 14?

answers: Both show that justice is not always revealed immediately or completely
Both prove that people control their destiny
Both concern only eating and drinking
medium.explanation: Oppressive rule, forgotten wicked people, and delayed judgment all display disorder and apparent injustice.
medium.q: How do delayed judgment and the rule of the wicked relate to the passage's theme?

answers: Everything in the world has no value at all
The forgetting of the wicked shows a troubling lack of lasting order and justice
challenge.explanation: The statement summarizes the troubling contrast between the wicked person's former prominence and his being forgotten.
challenge.q: What does "this is also vanity" mean in the context of verse 10?

answers: There is no difference between the righteous and the wicked
Judgment may be delayed, yet it will be well with those who fear God
challenge.explanation: Although judgment is delayed and life appears unjust, verse 12 affirms the ultimate good of fearing God.
challenge.q: What balance does Qohelet present between delayed judgment and faith?

answers: Both show a disorder between actions and their results
Both deal only with the limits of wisdom
challenge.explanation: Rule that harms others and outcomes that do not match conduct both reveal a distorted moral order.
challenge.q: What is the connection between harmful rule and the injustice described later?

easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions eating, drinking, and being merry.
easy.q: Which activities are mentioned in the verse?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says that mirth shall abide with him of his labour.
easy.q: What accompanies a person through his labor?

answers: Because simple joy accompanies a person amid uncertainty and labor
medium.explanation: In a world of uncertainty and apparent injustice, ordinary joy remains a good part of human life.
medium.q: Why does Qohelet commend joy in this chapter?

answers: Within the sphere of human life on earth
medium.explanation: The expression refers to life and activity in the earthly human realm.
medium.q: What does "under the sun" mean in this verse?

answers: Companionship throughout the days of one's life
medium.explanation: The verse says that mirth shall abide with a person during the days of his life.
medium.q: What does mirth provide according to the verse?

answers: Wait to live until everything is understood
Receive the simple good of life amid labor
challenge.explanation: Qohelet recommends eating, drinking, and being merry as appropriate goods within human labor.
challenge.q: What practical attitude emerges from verse 15?

answers: Joy gives control over every event
Joy enables a person to live his days without controlling all of life
challenge.explanation: Joy does not remove uncertainty; it accompanies a person while he lives within it.
challenge.q: How is joy related to the human limitations mentioned earlier?

answers: Joy is an ongoing companion, not merely a single event
Joy belongs only at the end of life
challenge.explanation: The wording presents mirth as something that remains with a person throughout his days of labor.
challenge.q: What does the phrase "shall abide with him" suggest?

paragraphs.title: The Limits of Wisdom and the Absence of Rest

answers: Wisdom and the work done upon the earth
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, "I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth."
easy.q: What did Qohelet apply his heart to know?

answers: All the work done under the sun
easy.explanation: Verse 17 says that a man cannot find out the work done under the sun.
easy.q: What can a man not find out?

easy.explanation: The passage says that even though a wise man seeks to know it, he shall not be able to find it.
easy.q: Can even a wise man find everything?

medium.explanation: The passage describes a person laboring to seek understanding, yet not finding it completely.
medium.q: What does the search for understanding require?

answers: Gain complete understanding of God's work
medium.explanation: The search concerns understanding the work done under the sun, not finding a physical object.
medium.q: What does "find" mean in the context of these verses?

answers: The search continues without rest, and even at night a person does not see everything
The search is possible only at night
medium.explanation: Verse 16 portrays continual concern, saying there is that which neither day nor night sees sleep with his eyes.
medium.q: How do day and night relate to the search?

answers: The wise man is forbidden to search
Wisdom cannot discover the whole work of God
A wise man can control everything that will happen
challenge.explanation: Even a wise person may labor to understand, but cannot find out the whole work done under the sun.
challenge.q: What limitation of wisdom is emphasized in verse 17?

answers: They explain why joy accompanies a person in labor instead of complete understanding
They cancel the value of eating and drinking
They state that labor does not exist
challenge.explanation: Since complete understanding cannot be attained, the simple joys of life remain meaningful companions in labor.
challenge.q: How do verses 16–17 connect with verse 15?

answers: Only an unwise person can understand life
Wisdom is valuable, but it has a boundary that cannot be crossed
challenge.explanation: Qohelet takes the pursuit of wisdom seriously while stressing that even the wise cannot understand everything.
challenge.q: What does "though a wise man think to know it" teach about wisdom?
